'''Nils G. Walter''' is an American chemist who is the Francis S. Collins Collegiate Professor of [[Chemistry]], [[Biophysics]], and [[Biochemistry|Biological Chemistry]] at the [[University of Michigan]], [[Ann Arbor]]. Research in the Nils Walter Lab focuses on [[non-coding RNA]] through the lens of single molecule techniques. He is the Founding Director of the Single Molecule Analysis in real-Time (SMART) Center at Michigan. In addition, Walter is the Founding Co-director for the University of Michigan Center for RNA Biomedicine whose mission is to enrich the university's intellectual and training environment around RNA Biomedicine. He served as associate director for the Michigan Post-baccalaureate Research Education Program (PREP) from 2015 to 2025.

== Education and early life ==
Nils G. Walter was born in 1966 in [[Frankfurt am Main]], [[Germany]]. He received his “Vordiplom” ([[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]]) and “Diploma” ([[Master's degree|Masters]]) from the [[Technical University of Darmstadt]] after performing research with {{Interlanguage link|Hans-Günther Gassen|de|Hans-Günther Gassen}} on the physicochemical characterization of a [[protein]] [[dehydrogenase]] enzyme. He is a Dr. Ing. ([[PhD]]) graduate from the Technical University of Darmstadt and the [[Max-Planck-Institute]] for Biophysical Chemistry where he studied molecular ''[[in vitro]]'' evolution of [[DNA]] and RNA using [[fluorescence]] techniques with Nobel laureate [[Manfred Eigen]]. For his postdoctoral studies, he turned to RNA enzymes under the guidance of John M. Burke at the [[University of Vermont]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Walter | first1=Nils G. | last2=Burker | first2=John M. | title=The hairpin ribozyme: Structure, assembly and catalysis | journal=Current Opinion in Chemical Biology | date=1998 | volume=2 | issue=1 | pages=24–30 | doi=10.1016/S1367-5931(98)80032-X | pmid=9667918 }}</ref>

== Career ==
The Nils Walter Lab studies both [[non-coding RNA]] and protein-coding RNAs, and how the former control the [[gene expression]] of the latter, using tools from biophysics, biochemistry, cell biology, molecular biology and chemical biology.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Walter|first=Nils G.|date=2015-04-01|title=Going viral: riding the RNA wave to discovery|journal=RNA|volume=21|issue=4|pages=756–757|doi=10.1261/rna.049403.114|issn=1469-9001|pmc=4371365|pmid=25780223}}</ref> Most prominently, the lab uses leading-edge single molecule and [[super-resolution microscopy]] and [[single-molecule FRET]] approaches to probe the diverse functional mechanisms of transcriptional and translational [[riboswitches]], the [[spliceosome]], the [[RNA silencing]] and [[RNA interference]] machinery, [[ribozymes]], as well as devices from [[DNA nanotechnology]], in vitro and in live cells.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Walter|first1=Nils G.|last2=Huang|first2=Cheng-Yen|last3=Manzo|first3=Anthony J.|last4=Sobhy|first4=Mohamed A.|date=2008-06-01|title=Do-it-yourself guide: how to use the modern single-molecule toolkit|journal=Nature Methods|volume=5|issue=6|pages=475–489|doi=10.1038/nmeth.1215|issn=1548-7105|pmc=2574008|pmid=18511916 |bibcode=2008NatMe...5..475W }}</ref><ref>{{Cite shed light on intracellular RNAs|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=114|issue=6|pages=3224–3265|doi=10.1021/cr400496q|issn=1520-6890|pmc=3968247|pmid=24417544}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Widom|first1=Julia R.|last2=Dhakal|first2=Soma|last3=Heinicke|first3=Laurie A.|last4=Walter|first4=Nils G.|date=2014-11-01|title=Single-molecule tools for enzymology, structural biology, systems biology and nanotechnology: an update|journal=Archives of Toxicology|volume=88|issue=11|pages=1965–1985|doi=10.1007/s00204-014-1357-9|issn=1432-0738|pmc=4615698|pmid=25212907|bibcode=2014ArTox..88.1965W }}</ref>

Walter is the author of more than 240 articles (h-index >70) and numerous patents and disclosures of invention,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mandal|first1=Shankar|last2=Li|first2=Zi|last3=Chatterjee|first3=Tanmay|last4=Khanna|first4=Kunal|last5=Montoya|first5=Karen|last6=Dai|first6=Liuhan|last7=Petersen|first7=Chandler|last8=Li|first8=Lidan|last9=Tewari|first9=Muneesh|last10=Johnson-Buck|first10=Alexander|last11=Walter|first11=Nils G.|date=2021-02-01|title=Direct kinetic fingerprinting for high-accuracy single-molecule counting of diverse disease biomarkers|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=54|issue=2|pages=388–402|doi=10.1021/acs.accounts.0c00621|pmid=33382587|pmc=8752314 }}</ref> including one on a new diagnostic single molecule counting approach termed SiMREPS that startup company aLight Sciences Inc. was founded to commercialize.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Johnson-Buck|first1=Alexander|last2=Su|first2=Xin|last3=Giraldez|first3=Maria D.|last4=Zhao|first4=Meiping|last5=Tewari|first5=Muneesh|last6=Walter|first6=Nils G.|date=2015-07-01|title=Kinetic fingerprinting to identify and count single nucleic acids|journal=Nature Biotechnology|volume=33|issue=7|pages=730–732|doi=10.1038/nbt.3246|issn=1546-1696|pmc=4559481|pmid=26098451}}</ref> He has been invited to speak at over 280 speaking engagements and is the Principal Investigator of two dozen current and past National Institutes of Health research grants and three dozen private foundation grants (see [https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/walter-lab/ Nils Walter Lab]).

He currently serves or has served on several editorial boards including [[Methods (journal)|Methods]], [[Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews]] (WIRES), [[Biopolymers (journal)|Biopolymers]] and the [[Journal of Biological Chemistry]], as well as being a guest editor for [[Chemical Reviews]], [[Encyclopedia of Biophysics]], and [[Methods in Enzymology]]. Walter has received numerous honors including the Jean Dreyfus Boissevain Lectureship of [[Trinity University (Texas)|Trinity University]], the Harold R. Johnson Diversity Service Award, the Imes and Moore Faculty Award, the Faculty Recognition Award of the [[University of Michigan]], the [[RNA Society]] Mid-Career Award, and the [[Biophysical Society]] Kazuhiko Kinosita Award in Single-Molecule Biophysics. He has been elected an [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS]] Fellow. Walter is a member of several professional organizations including the Society of German Chemists ([[GDCh]]), {{ill|German Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology|de|Gesellschaft für Biochemie und Molekularbiologie}} (GBM), the [[RNA Society]], the [[American Chemical Society]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and the [[Biophysical Society]].{{cn|date=August 2026}}
